meaning: Stripe can't find that price ID with the API key you used. Almost always the price exists in a different mode (test vs live) or a different Stripe account than the key.
causes: Price created in test mode but the app uses a live secret key, or the reverse.
Price ID copied from a different Stripe account or sandbox.
A product ID (prod_...) was used where a price ID (price_...) is required.
The price ID is hard-coded in code but env differs per environment.

steps.text: In Stripe Dashboard, check the mode toggle, open the product, and copy the price ID (price_...) shown under Pricing.
Compare it to your key: sk_test_ needs test prices, sk_live_ needs live prices. Recreate the product in live mode before going live.
Keep price IDs in env vars per environment instead of hard-coding them.
Quick check from a terminal using the same key.

prompt: Stripe checkout fails with 'No such price'. Move all Stripe price IDs into environment variables (STRIPE_PRICE_ID etc.), make sure the server uses the matching secret key for the same mode, and use price_ IDs not prod_ IDs in line_items. List every place a price or product ID is hard-coded.

faq.q: I switched to live and it broke?
faq.a: Test-mode products don't exist in live mode; recreate them in live and update the IDs.

faq.q: Can I use the price ID in the browser?
faq.a: Price IDs are not secret, but create the Checkout Session on the server with your secret key.
